request.description:
newMergedRuns always appends the subject run's records as the newest layer, even when an older run is the subject and a chronologically later prior run exists (the checkout-without-the-local-feed resolution). The later run that actually closed a tick loses row, owner and marker precedence to the older subject, so a closed row can show the ended run's attempt and tier rather than the closing run's. Tick cno fixed the state this produced; ordering the merge by the checkpoints' own UpdatedAt (with a defined tie-break) would fix the provenance too.
evidence: internal/statusmodel/epic.go newMergedRuns (runs = prior..., current always last); internal/cli/status_model.go priorRunsForEpic already orders the priors by UpdatedAt

ticfac run epic-hn6 created this tick by absorbing the finding c46fd55cda40b763f59f7cad87058d86e86a181fd4fda554d2fe8e8738e81141 (reported by run-epic-hn6/tick-cno/attempt-26): the finding was judged against the epic's definition of done and gates done item A3. The decision record — item id, verdict, observed or predicted, confidence — is .ticfac/runs/epic-hn6/absorptions/c46fd55cda40b763f59f7cad87058d86e86a181fd4fda554d2fe8e8738e81141.json on the run branch.
request.title: Merge orders the subject run last regardless of checkpoint chronology
